item.title: Lip Critic rode the Demonator straight to Theft World
item.description: Exclusive: When the Brooklyn band dropped Hex Dealer in 2024, they already had a follow-up record in the works—until Bret Kaser’s identity was stolen. Read our feature with the band and listen to “Legs In A Snare” below.

item.title: The lack of music in The moment only reveals the emptiness of its satire
item.description: CineMusic: Even with its many attempts at being tongue-in-cheek, Charli XCX’s new film doesn’t have much to say about pop stardom that hasn’t already been said before and dramatized more persuasively. It just prolongs brat past its cultural expiration date.

item.title: Good Luck, Have Fun, Don't Die is sci-fi as annoyingly quirky as its title
item.description: Gore Verbinski's AI-centric return to filmmaking, Good Luck, Have Fun, Don't Die is overly trendy, quirky, and predictable.

item.title: Pillion's Harry Lighton on his coming-of-kink film's "high-school transformation"
item.description: The A.V. Club spoke to Pillion filmmaker Harry Lighton about the locks, masks, and leather of his kinky romance.

item.title: Is Charley Crockett the only cowboy willing to resist country music's MAGA machine?
item.description: While Turning Point’s “All-American Halftime Show” parades country stars for the alt-right, Crockett is busy calling out the “cosplay president” and telling Nashville to take notes from Bad Bunny.

item.title: Melania's budget could've paid the salaries of every fired Washington Post employee, three times over
item.description: An incomplete breakdown of Jeff Bezos' financial priorities, weighing one piece of propaganda (Melania) against 300 journalists.

item.title: The Mummy (no, not Lee Cronin's The Mummy) will return in May 2028
item.description: Many mummies are making money moves at the movies. But only one Mummy movie has Brendan Fraser and Rachel Weisz.
